origin_result.basis: All checks passed: final manufacture took place in the UAE (PASS), manufacturing goes beyond minimal operations of Art. 3.5.1 (PASS), all 3 non-originating inputs classified outside subheading 761010 — CTSH (PASS), build-down 49.0% against threshold of 45% on FOB basis — VA (PASS). Totals: 6 inputs, of which 3 non-originating (51% of price).

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory before the certificate can be applied for: the factory must be located outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence, and provide a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added; registration takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the certificate: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload proof of factory registration and the commercial invoice (and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice), and submit the application; processing takes about one working day and the service runs 24/7.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000.
The competent authority issues the certificate before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import.

The exporter ships the goods directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar, and the exporter indicates third-party invoicing if the invoice is issued by a third party.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020 including which origin criterion is claimed, keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing, and answers a customs request within 10 working days.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate shown.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the rule CTSH + VA 45% is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022), not the official text.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
